The first release of Lucid, a web client for your CalDAV calendars and tasks that you run yourself: with a double-click on your own computer, or on a server for others.

- Month, week, day and agenda views with drag and drop, and tasks with checklists, priorities and repeats right beside them. On a busy day, its tasks share one entry so its events stay in sight.
- Repeating events and tasks: change or delete only one, this and the following ones, or all of them, undo a series change, and build repeats such as "every 2 weeks on Monday and Thursday" in a repeat editor.
- Time zones of their own for the events and tasks that need them, such as a flight from Berlin at 10:00 to New York at 13:00, while the calendar shows every time in yours.
- Dates and times can be typed as well as picked.
- Light and dark mode, English and German.
- A problem report that keeps your calendar private: it holds no titles, names or notes unless you add an item's content yourself.

## Before you start

Lucid 0.1 is for early adopters. It reads and writes your real calendars, so try it with a test calendar first. It is tested with Nextcloud; other CalDAV servers should work, and if yours doesn't, the problem report (account menu, **Report a problem**) tells us why. [Status and limits](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid#status-and-limits) lists what is missing, such as reminders and invitations.

## Known issues

- Lucid reads a time zone whose name it doesn't know, such as Outlook's "W. Europe Standard Time", as UTC: an invitation from Outlook can show an hour or two late in Berlin. Saving the event in Lucid keeps that zone ([#12](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid/issues/12)).

Not yet tried on a real machine: the double-click start on Windows and macOS, Safari, the Home Manager service on Ubuntu and the launchd agent on macOS. If you try one of them, please tell us how it went in [Discussions](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid/discussions).

## Install

- **On your own computer:** download the archive for your system below, extract it and double-click `lucid`.
- **On a server:** the container image `ghcr.io/tbckr/lucid:0.1.0`, the deb, rpm or Arch package below, or the NixOS module from `github:tbckr/lucid/stable`.

The [README](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid#quick-start) explains each.

## Upgrading from a release candidate

No setting changed. A package of 0.1.0 installs over the candidate's, the container image is `0.1.0` or `latest`, and with Nix, follow `github:tbckr/lucid/stable` instead of the candidate's tag.

Since rc.2, whose [notes](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid/releases/tag/v0.1.0-rc.2) say what changed since rc.1, events and tasks can have time zones of their own and dates and times can be typed. On a busy day or hour, tasks share one entry before events go behind "N more" or "+N", and entries can be dragged out of that list. The time grid moves and resizes in steps of 30 minutes instead of 15, and a new event lasts 30 minutes instead of an hour.

Also since rc.2:

- A single event or task that another app gave a time zone keeps it when you change it in Lucid; rc.2 could store its time in UTC instead.
- A repeating event or task from another time zone shows in that zone in the editor, where you change its repeat, and stays in it; rc.2 showed it on your days and moved an event series into your time zone.
- A series entered in the editor at a time summer time skips, such as 02:30 on the night Berlin changes to summer time, is saved at 03:30, where the calendar puts it too, and the editor says so before you save. rc.2 saved it at 01:30, so it repeated an hour early on every other day ([#10](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid/issues/10)).
- A changed repeat saved for all events moves the whole series onto it: a weekly series that started on a Tuesday, changed to Fridays from a later event, starts on the first Friday instead of keeping its first Tuesday, and the repeat editor says whether the event you edit moves or stays ([#11](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid/issues/11)).
- Lucid tells your CalDAV server who it is, with `lucid/0.1.0` as its user agent.

Lucid keeps nothing of its own, so a series that rc.2 saved an hour early or with its first event off the repeat stays that way on your server: check it and correct it in the editor.
